20.en: "To read the future, one must have the capacity to understand it, the will to shape it, and the strength to keep it safe."

38.en: Perfect knowledge of future events is the greatest power in the universe.

46.en: Protect the future by combatting those who seek to alter fate’s outcome.

54.en: Knowledge of the future must be treated like forbidden knowledge, kept secret and protected at all costs.

76.en: Seek out proven methods of divination. Collate and cross-reference their results to determine the most likely outcome of destiny. Guard these secrets closely; they must not fall into the wrong hands but use them to stay one step ahead of the enemy. Determine the best way to use this knowledge; careful nudges to affect critical moments.

82.en: Ocularians do not concern themselves with the present petty concerns of the Inquisition but are obsessed with the desire to foresee the future. Whatever divinatory methods an Ocularian chooses to use, they not only read the future but aim to manipulate it, ensuring that what comes to pass benefits the Imperium.

86.en: Ocularian Inquisitors are rare and long considered to operate only in the Calixis Sector of Segmentum Obscrurus. In part because when Ocularians travel across the galaxy for a rumoured divinatory tool or source of information, they do so secretly. The Macharian Sector contains numerous anomalies and sites of interest for Ocularian researchers, who study divinatory forms wherever possible, even if their sources are xenos.

90.en: While Ocularians are considered Radical, and their prophetic rituals borderline heretical, they are mostly tolerated. Ocularians keep the details of their practices a closely guarded secret, making their actions seem unpredictable to other Inquisitors. Only with their own do they discuss divinatory tools and methods, informing others only when they have warnings to impart.

94.en: Being accepted into the Ocularians involves much more than merely professing to share their beliefs, and many of those who are admitted into their ranks subsequently consider themselves superior to others within the Inquisition.

110.en: Ocularians are obsessive characters — they may appear easily detached from things happening around them, instead focused on their work and its outcomes.

118.en: Most Ocularians see themselves as protectors of the Imperium’s future, more important than the here and now. A calculated loss today that ensures a better future later is a loss graciously accepted.

126.en: Despite those points, Ocularians remain loyal to the Inquisition; the knowledge they glean is, after all, for their favour and the defence of the Imperium — even if they may appear aloof at times or the strangest of Radicals in the eyes of their peers.

140.en: The Ocularian Inquisitor’s compiled divinations speak of an Imperial saint coming to light on @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.AZrjjtrYpox78Zme]{Goros Pok}, one the people desperately need. But evidence of Tzeentchian cults on the planet suggests a likely opposition to this fate. Defeat the cult without causing any commotion, and heed the Inquisitor’s prophecies: ‘protect the severed hand’, ‘hide from the wings of the watcher’, and ‘three boats shall herald their arrival.

148.en: The Ocularian Inquisitor has uncovered a ring of heretics producing and selling blasphemous daemon-influenced Tarot. The characters must halt this corruption before it spreads further through the sector’s black markets. The trouble is, the blasphemous Tarot appears reliably divinatory, so the cult always appears to be a step ahead.
